categories.name: conjoined_directive
categories.definition: The phrase states, in full, a positive required action of the assistant that is coordinate with other requirements in the same passage — one conjunct of a compound instruction that survived only in part.
categories.boundary: Excludes manner_or_quality_qualifier, which modifies how an action already named is performed rather than naming a further action; and non_assistant_addressee, where the duty-bearer is a developer, OpenAI, the platform or the user.
examples: Extra care is required in agentic contexts
All applicable instructions must be followed
Assume earlier context remains relevant when plausible

categories.name: worked_example_particular
categories.definition: The phrase's referent is one of the Spec's illustrative dialogues: the facts of the hypothetical, the verdict on a candidate response, or the reason a response is labelled GOOD/BAD. It cannot be understood without that specific scenario.
categories.boundary: Excludes illustrative_instance, which is an example item inside a prose norm ('e.g., sending an email'), not a scenario with a labelled response.
examples: The free plan may meet the user's needs despite curiosity about upgrading and financial constraints.
The selected auto-apply option authorizes direct code changes in the user's editor.
The prohibited signature request serves the legitimate goal of speeding an insurance claim.

categories.name: descriptive_premise
categories.definition: A declarative statement with no deontic operator, asserting how the world, the models, users, developers or systems in fact are or may be — background the passage builds on.
categories.boundary: Excludes rationale_or_purpose (a fact offered as the norm's ground) and definition_or_constitution (a stipulation about a term's meaning).
examples: Users can always access a transparent experience through direct-to-consumer products
Available tools are documented by system or developer messages
Tool responses append role=tool messages and reinvoke the assistant

categories.name: prohibition_or_avoidance
categories.definition: The phrase's force is negative: a 'must not / never / do not / avoid / omit / rather than' constraint, including one item of an enumerated prohibition list. The negation is the content, not merely the wording.
categories.boundary: Excludes conjoined_directive (a positive required action) and scope_delimitation, which says what a prohibition covers rather than asserting the prohibition.
examples: System messages must not override root-level principles
Models should not autonomously whistleblow
Omission of detailed instructions, calculations, and strategic insights

categories.name: scope_delimitation
categories.definition: The phrase fixes the extension of a norm or term: which objects, media, parties, or ranges it covers, including restrictive 'only/just some' quantifiers and 'even when/always' hold-anyway markers. Answers 'over what does this range?'.
categories.boundary: Excludes applicability_condition (a triggering circumstance, not a domain) and illustrative_instance (items flagged as non-exhaustive examples rather than as the coverage itself).
examples: Access is to information from the models
Untrusted text is included
Only some calls cause side effects

categories.name: manner_or_quality_qualifier
categories.definition: The phrase attaches a qualitative or degree modifier to an act or its output — how, how much, in what style, to what standard ('briefly and respectfully', 'lucid, succinct', 'best-effort', 'without complaint', 'thorough and detailed').
categories.boundary: Excludes conjoined_directive (a separable action) and applicability_condition (a circumstance rather than a style). If deleting the phrase leaves the action intact but unstyled, it is manner.
examples: Information must be trustworthy
Prefer minimally disruptive approaches for users and non-users
Allowed discussion must use an objective point of view

categories.name: rationale_or_purpose
categories.definition: The phrase gives the why: a purpose clause ('to reduce surprises'), a justification ('because confirming every step is impractical'), a benefit, or a consequence offered in support of the norm.
categories.boundary: Excludes descriptive_premise, which asserts a fact the passage does not present as grounding the norm. Test: could it follow 'this is so because / in order to'?
examples: Mission to ensure artificial general intelligence benefits all humanity
Following the principles may not make sense in all cases
System level enables customization

categories.name: applicability_condition
categories.definition: The phrase supplies the antecedent that gates a statement: the if/when/unless/only-when circumstance under which the norm fires or the claim holds. Answers 'in what case?'.
categories.boundary: Excludes scope_delimitation, which fixes the entities, media or parties the norm ranges over rather than the triggering circumstance; and permission_or_exception, where the content is the licensed behaviour itself rather than the circumstance.
examples: The consequence occurs in an open market
A candidate instruction is not applicable when misaligned with an applicable higher-level instruction
Supersession occurs through a later message at the same level

categories.name: document_metatext
categories.definition: The phrase's referent is the Model Spec or the passage itself: its structure and section order, which version applies, what a passage introduces or lists, whether a list is exhaustive, the logical status of its items, cross-references to other sections or external policies, and what falls outside the document.
categories.boundary: Excludes illustrative_instance and scope_delimitation, which carry the passage's object-level content rather than talking about the passage.
examples: Models power OpenAI products, including the API platform
The document consists of direct instructions to the model
Definitions precede the chain of command, which precedes behavior principles

categories.name: permission_or_exception
categories.definition: The phrase's deontic force is permissive: a carve-out from a stated restriction ('except', 'unless', 'however ... may'), a grant of latitude, an optional alternative, or an explicit non-requirement.
categories.boundary: Excludes conjoined_directive and prohibition_or_avoidance, which require or forbid; and applicability_condition, which states when a permission applies rather than that it exists.
examples: Following the principles is not required, subject to Usage Policies
Developers receive broad latitude
Not exposed to users or developers except potentially in summarized form

categories.name: definition_or_constitution
categories.definition: The phrase fixes what a term denotes or what an entity is made of: it can be rewritten 'X is / means / consists of / also covers Y'. Includes statements of which parties a role-term ranges over, and definitional inclusions that extend a term's denotation.
categories.boundary: Excludes descriptive_premise, which asserts a contingent fact about how something behaves rather than stipulating the meaning of a term; and illustrative_instance, where the source flags the items as mere examples ('e.g.', 'such as') rather than as constitutive.
examples: Developer is the application developer
Developer may also be OpenAI
Content is a sequence of chunks

categories.name: precedence_or_preference_ordering
categories.definition: The phrase asserts a ranked relation between two or more things: authority levels, overriding, taking priority, 'preferred to', '>' orderings, and statements that something holds only as a defeasible default.
categories.boundary: Excludes temporal_or_procedural_order, which orders steps in time rather than in authority or desirability; and unresolved_tradeoff, where no winner is named.
examples: System ranks below root and above developer, user, and guideline
Later instructions at the same authority take precedence
Prefer assistant-reversible approaches over those requiring user reversal

categories.name: non_assistant_addressee
categories.definition: The norm, recommendation, capability or commitment attaches to someone other than the assistant — OpenAI, developers, administrators, the platform, or people generally.
categories.boundary: Excludes descriptive_premise, which reports what such parties typically do without normative force; and conjoined_directive, whose bearer is the assistant.
examples: A commitment to uphold additional principles in first-party direct-to-consumer products, including ChatGPT
People should have easy access
API developers and organization administrators are encouraged to follow the principles

categories.name: illustrative_instance
categories.definition: The phrase carries an item the source marks as illustrative or non-exhaustive — 'e.g.', 'such as', 'for instance', 'include(s)' — instantiating a general term retained elsewhere.
categories.boundary: Excludes scope_delimitation, where the enumeration is the norm's actual coverage; and document_metatext, which comments that a list is illustrative rather than carrying the items.
examples: Tokens include words or pieces of words
Evading shutdown is an example
Accumulated resources include compute, data, and credentials

categories.name: temporal_or_procedural_order
categories.definition: The phrase orders events or steps in time or in order of resort: 'before / after / first / then / precedes / wait until / only as a last resort'.
categories.boundary: Excludes precedence_or_preference_ordering (rank, not sequence). A phrase saying which of two things is better is precedence; one saying which comes first is sequence.
examples: Human review precedes any law-enforcement referral
Ask the user directly only when uncertainty persists.
After understanding, the user’s decision is respected

categories.name: unresolved_tradeoff
categories.definition: The phrase names two competing considerations and instructs or observes that they be weighed against each other, without naming a winner ('balance X against Y', 'several competing considerations').
categories.boundary: Excludes precedence_or_preference_ordering, which resolves the competition by ranking one side above the other.
examples: Balance maximizing legitimate access against minimizing real-harm risk
The assistant must balance acting with incomplete information against asking for clarification.
Weigh incorrect assumptions against the inconvenience of asking.

notes: Verification: a script checked that the 268 record ids in hole_corpus.json['missing'] appear exactly once across `assignments` (265) and `unclassified` (3), with no duplicates and no ids outside the corpus; the category counts plus the unclassified list sum to 268. Method: categories were induced by reading all 268 phrases with their clause_text, grouping by the semantic slot the lost fragment fills in its passage, then tightening boundaries until the pairwise tests below decided the hard cases. Judgement calls. (1) conjoined_directive is the closest thing to a residual bucket: nearly every phrase is grammatically a conjunct of something, so I restricted it to fragments that name a further *action* of the assistant and are not better read as a condition, style, exception, ordering or reason. (2) The applicability_condition / scope_delimitation line was the hardest recurring call; I settled on 'triggering circumstance' vs 'domain the norm ranges over', which puts 'even when adults could consent' and 'applies to text, audio and visual content' in scope, and 'when the user already has access' in condition. (3) rationale_or_purpose vs descriptive_premise turns on whether the passage offers the fact as ground for a norm; commentary blocks blur this, e.g. 'Providing all potentially misusable knowledge is impractical to avoid' is coded rationale because it licenses the policy that follows. (4) Default markers ('is the default') are coded precedence only when the defeasibility is the phrase's content; otherwise they are a secondary. (5) 'may' phrases in definition sections that fix who a role-term can denote ('Developer may also be OpenAI') were coded definition, not permission. Doubts the corpus raised. Three records (m0488#m209, #m210, #m211) are dispositional ascriptions of the assistant's character ('Appreciation for knowledge, beauty, and joy of discovery') with neither deontic force nor factual content nor an act to qualify; forcing them into descriptive_premise or manner_or_quality_qualifier would blunt both tests, so they are left unclassified rather than given a category of three. Also note the corpus's own caveat: every phrase is the read-back judge's paraphrase, so the taxonomy describes the shapes that judge noticed and how it chose to render them. Two systematic artefacts of that are visible: nominalised renderings ('Prohibition on persuading the user', 'Avoidance of deceptive behavior') that make deontic force a matter of the judge's wording, and one-record-per-conjunct splitting of enumerations ('hide communications' / 'symptoms' / 'supplies' as three records), which inflates prohibition_or_avoidance and scope_delimitation relative to how many distinct holes there really are. Cross-cutting observation not captured by the primary labels: worked_example_particular loss is total in kind rather than partial — for the Spec's illustrative dialogues the compression retains a label and the entire scenario, verdict and reasoning are lost, whereas for prose passages what survives is the bare act and what falls out is its condition, degree, exception and reason.
